title: Wasim Akram Hails Sri Lanka as a World-Class Travel Destination
byline: Former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram has described Sri Lanka as one of the world’s finest holiday destinations, praising the island’s natural beauty and his long-standing connection with the country.

title: Messi’s father recovering from 'health issue': family
byline: Lionel Messi’s father is recovering from an unspecified ’’health issue’’, the Argentina star’s family said Thursday, appealing for privacy after a flurry of recent media reports.

title: Over 1,200 killed in road accidents in less than six months
byline: The Sri Lanka Police has reported that 1,297 people were killed in road accidents across the country between January 1 and June 16, 2026.

title: No price hike for vehicles already imported by May 15: Deputy Minister
byline: Labour Minister and Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando says there is no possibility of increasing prices for vehicles that had already been imported to the country by May 15.

title: Three types of cardiac stents withdrawn immediately due to safety concerns
byline: The Medical Supplies Division (MSD) have ordered the immediate withdrawal of three types of ’inferior’ cardiac stents and instructed hospitals across Sri Lanka to isolate all remaining stocks without using them, in a major nationwide safety alert affecting heart treatment services.

title: Sri Lanka, India recognize urgency, but no result on implementation yet
byline: In the wake of the West Asian or Middle East crisis, Sri Lanka and India have recognized the need for the expeditious implementation of the Trincomalee petroleum hub project for energy security, but no specific timeline is carved out yet, Daily Mirror learns.

title: Shoe garland hung on MP Archuna’s portrait in Jaffna
byline: A shoe garland has been placed on a portrait of Member of Parliament Archuna Ramanathan in Jaffna.

title: Direct Ahmedabad-Colombo flights to begin, boosting tourism and business travel
byline: Direct flights between Ahmedabad and Colombo are set to begin this week, offering travellers from India’s Gujarat state easier access to Sri Lanka while reducing the need for connecting flights through Mumbai and Delhi.

title: Water Supply disrupted in Mahara and Gampaha until Saturday morning
byline: Water supply to the Mahara Pradeshiya Sabha and Gampaha Pradeshiya Sabha areas has been suspended from today (June 19) until 8.00 a.m. on Saturday (June 20) due to a sudden rupture in the main water supply line near the Kadawatha Central Expressway.

title: Indonesia to halt free meal scheme during holidays
byline: Indonesia will suspend its free meal scheme during holiday periods, after mass protests in the capital condemned wasteful spending and demanded that the goverment address worsening economic conditions.

title: Andy Burnham’s election to parliament sets up bid to oust UK PM Starmer
byline: Labour mayor Andy ​Burnham cleared a path to ousting British Prime Minister Keir Starmer after winning a parliamentary seat in northern England on Friday in what could be most consequential ‌local election in more than six decades.

title: Investigation Board appointed over Kalpitiya Range incident
byline: special Board of Inquiry has been appointed by the Commander of the Sri Lanka Air Force (SLAF) to investigate a confrontation that occurred between Air Force personnel and a group of individuals, including a police officer, during a bomb disposal exercise at the Kalpitiya field firing range on June 17.

title: World Cup Matchweek 2: Qualification Race Heats Up
byline: The opening matchweek of the 2026 FIFA World Cup is complete, and the race for places in the newly expanded Round of 32 is already heating up. With 12 group winners, 12 runners-up and the eight best third-placed teams advancing, every point could prove crucial.

title: US lifts naval blockade as Iran’s supreme leader says Trump made deal ’out of desperation’
byline: The US has dropped its naval blockade of Iran after the two countries signed a deal to end the war in the Middle East.

title: Iran war casts fresh shadow over Sri Lanka’s recovery
byline: Sri Lanka’s fragile economic recovery faces renewed external headwinds after Fitch Ratings downgraded its outlook on a growing number of emerging market sectors, warning that the ongoing Iran conflict is

title: ‘Two leaves and a bud’ becoming fiction as climate change hits tea: Dilmah Chief
byline: The centuries-old standard that defines premium Ceylon Tea is at risk of becoming “a fiction” as climate extremes disrupt growing conditions across Sri Lanka’s tea lands, Dilmah Tea Chairman and Chief

title: Ample world inventories may soften El Nino food supply shock
byline: A super El Nino is likely to unsettle global weather and threaten food output in the coming months, but near record world inventories, expectations ​of near-normal conditions in some key producing regions and advanced planning could limit the fallout.

title: New Directors appointed to 17 key healthcare institutions
byline: The Ministry of Health and Media has appointed new directors to 17 key healthcare institutions, with Health and Media Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa stating that policy decisions to strengthen the healthcare sector will be based on long-term national development rather than short-term political considerations.

title: Fisheries Ministry aids cyclone-affected fishermen
byline: Fishermen affected by Cyclone Ditwah in the Jaffna, Mullaitivu, and Mannar districts received boats and fishing nets under a recovery assistance programme at a special ceremony held at the Sea Nor Boat Factory premises in Karainagar.

title: No vaccine, conflict, mistrust: Ebola’s return to DR Congo
byline: Ebola is spreading again in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where conflict, mistrust and the lack of a vaccine have made the outbreak hard to contain.

title: Govt clarifies new import monitoring rules
byline: The Deputy Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said that the primary objective of the newly issued gazette notification is to systematically monitor import operations rather than impose restrictions on them.

title: President’s Fund provides laptops to 14 university students
byline: The President’s Fund yesterday provided laptop computers to 14 university students selected from applications submitted through Divisional Secretariat offices across the country.

title: Sri Lanka tightens import remittance regulations
byline: The Government has introduced new regulations aimed at strengthening the monitoring of outward remittances linked to import transactions through a Gazette Extraordinary issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No. 1 of 1969.

title: Sri Lanka could save billions by expanding EV use, says Energy Minister
byline: Sri Lanka could save billions of rupees spent on fossil fuel imports by increasing the use of electric vehicles (EVs) and charging them with renewable energy, Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka said.

title: Sri Lanka welcomes US-Iran ceasefire agreement
byline: The Government of Sri Lanka has welcomed the recently signed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the United States and the Iran, which establishes an immediate ceasefire between the two countries.

title: Kala Wewa renovation begins to stop water leaks
byline: The long-delayed renovation of the historic Kala Wewa Reservoir to permanently stop water leakages that have continued for more than 42 years officially commenced on June 16, with authorities assuring that the project will not disrupt cultivation or pose any safety risks.

title: Thirty-five killed as gunmen attack Niger’s biggest airport
byline: Thirty-five people have been killed after gunmen struck Niger’s largest airport on Thursday, officials say - the second attack in less than five months.

title: Mexico beat South Korea 1-0, become first team to reach World Cup knockouts
byline: FIFA World Cup 2026 cohosts Mexico became the first team to reach the knockout rounds with a 1-0 win over South Korea at a delirious Guadalajara Stadium on Thursday.

title: Switzerland says US-Iran talks planned for Friday are off
byline: Talks that had been planned for ​Friday between the ‌United States and Iran at the Burgenstock mountaintop ​resort in Switzerland ​will not take place, ⁠according to a ​Swiss foreign ministry statement.

title: Archchuna removes slipper-garlanded cut-out of himself
byline: Jaffna District MP Archchuna Ramanathan was seen removing a life-size cut-out of himself that had been decorated with a garland made of slippers and placed by the roadside in the Gurunagar area of Jaffna.

title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 18 as Israel says four soldiers killed by Hezbollah
byline: At least 18 people have been killed in southern Lebanon following a series of Israeli air strikes overnight, the country’s health ministry has said - while the Israeli military says four of its soldiers were also killed.

title: ’The last ride’: Trump takes final flight on old Air Force One
byline: ’’I was honoured to be aboard Air Force One last night on its final flight,’’ Monica Crowley, the US chief of protocol, said on X.

title: US-Iran talks postponed as Vance pulls out of Switzerland trip
byline: A new round of direct talks between the US and Iran have been postponed after Vice-President JD Vance delayed a planned trip to Switzerland.

title: Sri Lanka’s Liberal Youth Movement joins global liberal youth federation
byline: The Liberal Youth Movement (LYM) of Sri Lanka has secured official membership in the International Federation of Liberal Youth (IFLRY), marking a significant milestone for youth-led civic engagement in the country.

title: Sri Lankan Rupee appreciates further against US Dollar
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee appreciated further against the US Dollar today (19), with the selling rate falling to Rs. 338 compared to Thursday’s exchange rate.

title: Dengue cases rise to 44,480 with 28 deaths reported this year
byline: Health authorities have recorded 44,480 dengue cases across Sri Lanka so far this year, with 28 deaths reported due to the disease.

title: SJB has no issues with Dayasiri: MP
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has no issues with MP Dayasiri Jayasekera as he is not a member of that party, SJB MP Chathura Gallappathi said today.

title: Lanka Salt Company GM arrested over Rs. 14.3M corruption allegation
byline: The current General Manager of Lanka Salt Company has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over extensive corruption charges.

title: Ample world inventories may soften El Nino food supply shock
byline: A super El Nino is likely to unsettle global weather and threaten food output in the coming months, but near record world inventories, expectations ​of near-normal conditions in some key producing regions and advanced planning could limit the fallout.

title: Delayed peace deal weighs on CSE as profit-taking pulls indices lower
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange ended Friday’s session in negative territory, reversing early gains as delays surrounding the formal signing of the peace agreement between the United States and Iran dampened investor sentiment. title: ICC Chairman meets Dissanayake
byline: A meeting between President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and Mr Jay Shah, Chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC), was held this afternoon (19) at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Israel, Hezbollah agree to ceasefire starting on Friday - US official
byline: Israel and Hezbollah have ​agreed to a ‌ceasefire set to begin at 4 ​p.m. local time ​on Friday, a senior ⁠U.S. official ​told Reuters.

title: Colombo Bank legal officer arrested for alleged theft
byline: A 47-year-old female lawyer attached to the legal division of a Colombo-based commercial bank was arrested last night (18) at a supermarket in Ratmalana while allegedly attempting to steal multiple items.

title: ICC chief Jay Shah to meet Sri Lanka President Dissanayake
byline: International Cricket Council (ICC) chairman Jay Shah will arrive here on Friday on a whistle-stop tour and meet Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, with the SLC interim committee issue expected to be high on the agenda, government sources said.

title: Over 40 arrested in Walana STF raid on massage centres
byline: A total of 43 individuals have been arrested following a series of raids carried out by the Walana Central Anti-Vice Strike Force on massage centres in the Thalawathugoda area.

title: G.C.E. O/L examination results released online
byline: The Department of Examinations has released the results of the General Certificate of Education (Ordinary Level) Examination online. Students can now access their results over the internet.

title: Fire destroys processed tea stock at Elpitiya tea factory
byline: A fire broke out at a tea factory located at Wathurawila Junction on the Elpitiya–Mapalagama Road this evening, causing extensive damage to the premises.

title: Italy cancels US visit after Trump says Meloni ‘Begged’ him for photo
byline: Italy’s foreign minister has canceled a planned visit to the United States over comments President Donald Trump made about Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni earlier this week.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026: The First Round Is Complete. Here Are All the Stories That Matter.
byline: Germany ran riot. Spain was shocked. Messi showed that age is only a number. A complete match-by-match breakdown of every game across the opening round of the biggest World Cup in history.
